title: Process Identity
description: Schema for the process-identity sub-block of L2 Business Process entries. CR-BP-03 §8. The identity sub-block tests a process by name + description + trigger + outcome + evidence, not by name alone. A process may be poorly named but correctly described, or correctly named but mis-classified; the identity contract requires both, and provides evidence links to support review.

verb.description: Action verb (imperative; singular; TitleCase). E.g. Manage, Deliver, Onboard, Operate, Design, Govern. The verb should match the verb in the process name (the name is typically `<verb> <object>`).

object.description: The noun being acted on (TitleCase). E.g. Customer, Service, Order, Portfolio, Data, Risk. The object should match the noun in the process name.

scope.description: Optional scope qualifier. E.g. (Enterprise), (Tier-1), (Cloud), (GDPR). When the parent process is specialized for a specific scope (e.g. by customer segment, by region, by tier), the scope is captured here as well as in process_specialization + specialization_pattern.

outcome_statement.description: Outcome statement (the description-of-record). Describes what the process achieves — not what it does. The outcome_statement is the basis for the contribution report (CR-BP-03 §9) and the re-landscape check (BP-ARC-ID-004). Should reference a measurable outcome or state change, not a list of activities.

type.description: Type of evidence. documentation = internal docs; governance = governance artifacts (policies, charters); interview = SME interview notes; artifact = operational artifacts (logs, reports, process-mining output); standard = external standards (ITIL, BPMN, etc.); regulation = regulatory references.

ref.description: Reference (URL, document path, interview identifier, or artifact identifier).

evidence_links.description: Evidence links supporting the identity sub-block. The contribution report (CR-BP-03 §9) cross-checks the identity against this evidence.
